page.title: Traceability Matrix
page.purpose: Answer, for one scenario, whether its stated intent is proven: which operational targets are backed by requirements, which requirements are proven by live evidence, and where the unproven risk sits — with every verdict one interaction away from the evidence behind it.

priorities.statement: The overall verdict — is this scenario's business contract healthy, and how large is the debt — is answerable at first glance.
Unproven and failing requirements surface before healthy detail and registry bookkeeping.
Every verdict is one interaction away from the evidence that justifies it.
The status vocabulary (planned, in-progress, complete, failing, unproven) is legible without a legend.

states.description: No scenario chosen yet; the page guides selection instead of presenting a dead end.
Matrix for the chosen scenario is being fetched.
Matrix rendered: operational-target groups with requirement rows, statuses, and live evidence.
A requirement's detail drawer is open: evidence detail plus manual attestation.
Scenario chosen but its registry has no requirements.
Matrix fetch failed; cause stated, path forward offered.
Evidence is degraded (e.g. syncer unavailable); verdicts are marked reduced-confidence rather than silently overstated.

elements.name: Scenario
elements.description: Choose which scenario's contract to inspect; remembers recents.
INTENT, not yet built: a single at-a-glance verdict of contract health (e.g. proven/total with debt emphasis).
INTENT, partially built: the count of unproven requirements, exposed as a status — today a decorative chip without the number.
Registry bookkeeping (module/requirement/target counts). Belongs after the problems, not before them.
Per-requirement drill-in affordance opening the detail drawer.
INTENT: the drill-in drawer announced as a dialog; today an unannounced overlay div.
Reduced-confidence notice when evidence is degraded.

claims.statement: A single overall verdict of contract health is perceivable without scanning the groups.
claims.rationale: Priority 1. The current build computes group/unproven data but never rolls it up into one glanceable verdict.

claims.statement: When unproven requirements exist, that signal is exposed as a status element assistive tech announces, not a decorative chip.
claims.rationale: Reconciliation fixture must use a scenario with unproven requirements (bas/ seed concern, not a spec concern).

claims.statement: The unproven/problem signal reads before registry bookkeeping; counts of modules are never the first thing communicated.
Every requirement row offers a drill-in affordance to its detail and evidence.
Drilling into a requirement is fully keyboard operable.
The requirement detail drawer is announced as a dialog when it opens, not silently overlaid.
A failed matrix fetch is surfaced as an alert with the cause stated.
Degraded evidence is always visibly disclosed; the matrix never overstates confidence.
Arriving without a scenario renders dedicated guidance, not a blank or broken surface.
A scenario with no requirements renders a dedicated empty state.
The no-scenario guidance offers a concrete next step (recent scenarios, or the fleet view), never a dead-end sentence.
The empty-registry state points at the scaffolding wizard as the way forward.
planned, in-progress, complete, and failing are visually distinct from one another without a legend.
claims.rationale: The current tone mapping flattens planned and in-progress into identical neutral chips.

claims.statement: The number of unproven requirements is stated numerically, not merely flagged.
claims.rationale: The count is computed in the current build and then never rendered.

claims.statement: The matrix for a chosen scenario is shareable and deep-linkable by URL.
P0 groups and unproven rows visually outweigh healthy P2 detail; risk is where the eye lands first.
claims.rationale: Becomes checkable with the P2 saliency tier (importance ranking, never fake seconds).

verdict-headline.note: PLANNED — element does not exist in the current build; its absence is the expected reconciliation finding for verdict-at-a-glance.

unproven-signal.note: PLANNED — current build renders an unnamed chip with no count and no status role.

requirement-drawer.note: Exists, but as an unannounced div — the dialog role is the intent.

regions.note: OT groups, risk-first ordering; drawer opens from rows.
Registry counts live BELOW the content they describe — inverted from the current build.

x-spike.verdict-source: Operator judgment: business-health UX is directionally correct but unpolished — exactly what experience-manager must detect.
x-spike.notes: registry-summary is bound but is a plain div today; if reconciliation cross-checks its region role, that extra finding is genuine (bookkeeping unlabelled for AT), not spec error.
